interface.title: Microbiology Data Analysis Tool (Streamlit)
interface.field: Microbiology (bacterial growth, plate counts, antibiotic susceptibility)
interface.stage_of_work: Analysing and reporting results after an experiment
interface.what_it_is_for: You upload a small CSV or Excel table of bacterial counts. The app removes rows with missing values, works out from the column names whether it is a growth curve, a plate colony count or an antibiotic-vs-control comparison, and then shows the matching statistics, plots and a written summary, which you can download as a TXT or PDF report.

data.note: I uploaded all four test files through the sidebar uploader: sample_dataset.csv (growth curve, 8 time points), sample_colony_data.csv (6 plates), sample_antibiotic.csv (7 time points, control vs antibiotic) and colony_data_with_missing_and_outlier.csv (plate C has no count; plate E = 312 is an outlier). The uploader holds one file at a time, so a new upload replaces the old one. The app never crashed after an upload.

features.name: Auto-detecting dataset analyser
features.general: Load a table, have the tool work out what kind of experiment it is from its column names, and show the matching headline statistics and plots
features.specific: Upload a CSV, see the 'Detected Dataset Type' banner (Growth Curve / Colony Count / Antibiotic Comparison), four st.metric cards, the type-specific plot and, for growth and colony data, a distribution histogram
steps: Upload a file in the sidebar
Read the four metric cards for that type
Look at the type-specific plot (line, bar, or control-vs-treated line) and, where shown, the distribution histogram
serves_tasks: Compare a treated group with a control

features.name: Clean-and-flag preview (raw vs cleaned tables)
features.general: Drop incomplete records on load, say how many were removed, and let the user compare the original table with the cleaned one
features.specific: A 'Removed N rows containing missing/empty values' warning, with 'View Raw Data' and 'View Cleaned Data' expanders (the cleaned table keeps the original row indices, so you can see a row is missing)
steps: Expand View Raw Data to find the blank cell (None)
Compare with View Cleaned Data, where that index is missing

Compare the original data with the cleaned data

features.name: Analysis report export (TXT/PDF)

features.specific: The Generate Report section's Download Text Report and Download PDF Report buttons. They write microbiology_report.txt/.pdf with the date, detected type, the Experiment Summary and the Statistical Details. They only appear once a type has been detected.

not_done: The table toolbar's 'Download as CSV' did not produce a file, from either the raw table or the fullscreen cleaned table (screens/015.webp, screens/034.webp). This headless browser probably does not support that save path.
I could not read the PDF report's contents (it is binary, 1759 bytes). I only confirmed that it downloaded for the growth-curve and antibiotic datasets.
The outlier in colony_data_with_missing_and_outlier.csv (plate E = 312) is not flagged or excluded. The app has no control for this, so it inflates the mean (90.8) and SD (123.70) (screens/028.webp).
The text report for the file with a missing value does not say that a row was removed. Only the on-screen warning flags it.
I only checked chart fullscreen on the growth plot (screens/017.webp). The plots are static matplotlib images with no interactive zoom or hover.

The data table toolbar (click a header to sort, Search with '2 results', Show/hide columns, Fullscreen; screens/010.webp, screens/011.webp, screens/012.webp, screens/014.webp, screens/033.webp) worked, but it is generic Streamlit dataframe chrome, so it is not listed as a feature of this interface.

I only switched the theme (Dark, then back to Light, screens/031.webp) and collapsed and reopened the sidebar (screens/032.webp). These are generic Streamlit chrome, so I did not treat them as features. I did not try Rerun, Auto rerun, Clear cache, Print or Record screen in the main menu.
